evidenceBoundary: Static inspection and deterministic scripted-provider tests only. No live cloud inference was invoked.
problemRecovered: run_command treated every completed process as successful, even when the terminal supplied a nonzero exit code.
The duplicate supervisor treated all run_command calls as mutating, including command-classifier-proven read-only inspections.
The generic terminal tool-loop exit was terminal but did not create the normal no-progress receipt.

change.exitStatus: A nonzero terminal exit is now a TOOL_EXECUTION_FAILED tool result with the redacted Exit code and command output retained in the diagnostic.
change.readOnlyCommands: Only a parsed run_command whose existing conservative classifier returns read-only enters duplicate suppression. Other commands remain non-suppressible and state-changing.
change.loopObservability: Three identical consecutive tool requests and six-turn oscillations record a no-progress interruption in the ledger and return an efficiency receipt before blocking.

proven: A nonzero shell-process exit cannot be presented to the runtime as a successful tool result.
A repeated classifier-proven read-only terminal inspection executes once, replays its authoritative result once, and records the avoided dispatch in the ledger.
A repeated failed classifier-proven read-only terminal inspection physically executes at most twice before the run blocks with an AGENT_TOOL_LOOP_DETECTED receipt and ledger interruption.
Mutating and unclassified commands do not become suppressible through model-provided arguments.
notProven: Live-model improvement in tool selection, retries, token use, or completion rate.
Browser-tool, external-tool, or general unnecessary-chain reduction beyond the governed command and duplicate-read surface.
Packaged desktop terminal UX or Windows console visibility.
requiredNextEvidence: Run paired live free-route engineering tasks under the same repository, route, budget, verifier, and completion criteria. Record command exit results, duplicate suppression, retries, token receipts, and verification outcomes; preserve route or quota unavailability as a blocker.
